meta.audience: The assembled peoples of Zarahemla, Nephi, and Limhi

world_behind.title: The arithmetic, given once and never repeated
world_behind.text: The people of Zarahemla outnumber the descendants of Nephi, and the two together are less than half the Lamanites. The ruling group is a minority inside a minority, and the record supplies the figures as an aside before the assembly begins.

world_behind.title: Why everybody ends up called Nephites
world_behind.text: The throne could pass only through one line, and the record treats that single constitutional fact as sufficient to settle what an entire population is called. The label is political rather than genealogical, and it is explained in a subordinate clause.

world_behind.title: A record read aloud to a nation
world_behind.text: Two first-person accounts of colonies that left and came back, read out by a king to an assembly. Everything the reader has spent sixteen chapters on becomes public knowledge inside the story at this moment, and the people hearing it are hearing it for the first time.

world_behind.title: Amulon's children, two generations on
world_behind.text: The twenty-four women carried off from Shemlon had children. Those children are displeased with what their fathers did, refuse to carry their fathers' names, and ask to be counted as Nephites. The record has followed that abduction from the raid to the next generation.

world_behind.title: A king granting religious authority
world_behind.text: Mosiah gives Alma the power to establish congregations throughout the land and to ordain over them. The permission runs from the crown and the ordaining runs from Alma. The record states the arrangement plainly and never raises the question of how the two authorities sit together.

world_behind.title: Membership by application
world_behind.text: In a society where standing runs by descent and the throne runs by descent, verse 23 makes belonging to the people of God a matter of wanting it. Whosoever were desirous joined, and the record supplies no other qualification.

words.text: A grouping of people, used here as a plain organizational term. The assembly forms in two of them at the start of the chapter, and by verse 21 the congregations are meeting in different ones. The same word carries a national division and then a church structure.

Defiled, made unclean, in the ritual sense rather than the modern environmental one. The people apply it to the Lamanites' spiritual condition and pair it with "sinful." What follows is pain and anguish for their souls.

Counted into a group, enrolled. The record uses it of the people of Zarahemla joining the Nephites and, a verse earlier, of Amulon's children asking to be counted among them. Both are administrative acts with a census verb, and both change what a person is called.

To urge strongly, to press a point on someone who already knows it. Alma exhorts the people of Limhi to remember that it was the Lord who delivered them. They had been there; the exhortation is against forgetting.

To appoint to an office with authority attached. Mosiah grants Alma the power to do it throughout the land, which makes a king the source of the permission and Alma the source of the ordination. The record does not comment on the arrangement.

Did well, thrived. It is the last word of the chapter's last clause, after the Spirit poured out and the blessing. In this record the word is usually a hinge, and what follows here is a chapter about a generation that would not believe.

phrases.term: His people who tarried in the land were struck with wonder and amazement
phrases.text: The audience defined by what it did not do. These are the ones who never went up to the land of Nephi with Zeniff, hearing for the first time what became of those who did. The next verse adds that they knew not what to think. The reaction has not yet become an opinion.

phrases.term: Even shed many tears of sorrow
phrases.text: The second of five reactions, and the only one with a physical sign attached. The occasion is thinking about the brethren the Lamanites had slain. The phrase occurs once in scripture.

An unusual adjective for goodness, and it appears once in scripture. What they are responding to is timing: Alma's people were delivered out of Lamanite hands the morning after the promise. The word marks how quickly the answer came.

phrases.term: Pain and anguish for the welfare of their souls
phrases.text: The fifth reaction, and the only one directed at somebody else. They think about the Lamanites, call the state sinful and polluted, and then feel this. Three chapters later the sons of Mosiah will describe their own missionary motive in almost the same emotional terms.

phrases.term: They would no longer be called by the names of their fathers
phrases.text: Children repudiating a name rather than a doctrine. They were displeased with the conduct, and the remedy they chose was to take up a different name and be counted elsewhere. Nothing is said about whether their fathers were still living.

phrases.term: Neither could they all hear the word of God in one assembly
phrases.text: A logistical constraint given as the reason for a religious structure. The verse pairs it with there being too many for one teacher. Both halves are about capacity, and the phrase is unique in scripture.

phrases.term: Notwithstanding there being many churches they were all one church
phrases.text: The claim that holds the arrangement together, and it occurs once in scripture. The verse gives the test immediately: nothing was preached in any of them except repentance and faith in God. Unity is defined by content rather than by governance.

phrases.term: Whosoever were desirous to take upon them the name of Christ
phrases.text: Admission by wanting it. In a chapter that has just spent two verses sorting people by descent, this sentence opens a category that descent has nothing to do with. The record then names what they were called: the people of God.

verses.label: v. 1–4
verses.title: Everyone counted
verses.text: Everyone gathered, and the record pauses to count: Zarahemla's people outnumber Nephi's, and the Lamanites outnumber both by more than two to one. Then the assembly forms in two bodies, which is how they still think of themselves at the start of the chapter.

verses.label: v. 5–6
verses.title: Both records, read out
verses.text: Zeniff's account from departure to return, and Alma's account of the afflictions, from departure to return. The parallel construction is exact, and the two documents are given equal standing without comment.

verses.label: v. 7–11
verses.title: What they thought about, and felt
verses.text: Wonder and amazement, then joy at the delivered, then tears for the slain, then thanks for the speed of the rescue, then pain and anguish for the Lamanites' souls. Each begins "when they thought," and each has a different object. The sequence ends outside itself.

verses.label: v. 12–13
verses.title: Two changes of name
verses.text: Amulon's children take the name of Nephi because they are ashamed of their fathers. A whole second population takes it because of who may hold the throne. One renaming is a moral choice and the other is a legal consequence, and they are reported in consecutive verses without any transition between them.

verses.label: v. 14–18
verses.title: A king yields the floor
verses.text: Mosiah finishes and asks Alma to speak. Alma goes from body to body preaching repentance and faith, exhorts the delivered to remember who delivered them, and then baptizes Limhi and his people after the manner of the waters of Mormon.

verses.label: v. 19–22
verses.title: Divided, and not divided
verses.text: The king grants the power, Alma ordains, seven congregations form for reasons of capacity, and the record insists they are one because the preaching is the same. The unity claim is made about content, not about structure.

verses.label: v. 23–24
verses.title: A category not based on descent
verses.text: Whoever wanted the name took it and joined, and they were called the people of God. Then the Spirit poured out, and they were blessed and prospered. That is the sentence this record generally puts just before something goes wrong.

chapter.title: The record inside the record becomes public
chapter.text: Sixteen chapters of Zeniff's colony and Alma's flight are read aloud to everybody at once. Until this moment those events were known to the people who lived them; afterward they belong to the nation, and the next four chapters depend on that.

chapter.title: Five reactions, catalogued, and the last one travels
chapter.text: Wonder, joy, grief, thanks, and then pain and anguish for the welfare of Lamanite souls. Four are about themselves and the fifth is not. Three chapters later the sons of Mosiah give that fifth reaction as their reason for going.

chapter.title: The same phrase Abinadi produced in a courtroom
chapter.text: "Wonder and amazement" occurs three times in scripture. Twice are in this book: Noah's priests hearing Abinadi, and this assembly hearing the account of him read out. The record reuses the words without remarking on it.

chapter.title: "Nephite" is redefined as a political term
chapter.text: The people of Zarahemla are numbered with the Nephites for a stated constitutional reason: the kingdom went only to Nephi's descendants. From here on the label in this book names a citizenship.

chapter.title: The abduction chain closes
chapter.text: Noah's priests took twenty-four women in chapter 20; those women pleaded for their husbands' lives in chapter 23; here their children refuse the family name. Five chapters, two generations, and the record follows it to the end without moralizing at any stage.

chapter.title: The reason given for seven churches is capacity
chapter.text: Too many for one teacher, too many for one assembly. The organization is presented as a practical response to growth, and the theological claim, that they are all one church, is attached afterward and rests on what gets preached.

chapter.title: A society sorted by descent opens a category sorted by desire
chapter.text: Two verses on lineage are followed immediately by admission to the people of God on the basis of wanting the name. The record puts these next to each other and lets the contrast stand.

chapter.title: Role in the book
chapter.text: Mosiah 9 through 24 was an inserted record; this chapter rejoins the main narrative and reassembles everyone in one place. What it sets up is immediate: a rising generation that did not hear Benjamin, Alma the younger, the sons of Mosiah, and the end of the kings.

applications.title: Read the account out loud
applications.text: Mosiah did not summarize; he read both records start to finish to everyone at once. When a shared history matters, letting people hear the primary document beats hearing your version of it.

applications.title: Notice which reaction points outward
applications.text: Four of the five responses were about the assembly's own experience. The fifth was about somebody else's soul, and it is the one that produced action years later. Watch for the feeling that is not about you.

applications.title: Name what you are grateful for precisely
applications.text: They gave thanks for the immediate goodness of God: for how fast the answer came. Specific gratitude is harder to manufacture and easier to trust.

applications.title: A shared name can be refused
applications.text: Amulon's children could not undo what their fathers did, and they could decline to carry it forward. Where you have inherited something you did not choose, the question is what you agree to keep calling yourself.

applications.title: Divide for capacity, unite on content
applications.text: Seven groups because seven were needed, and one church because the preaching was the same. When a thing outgrows its structure, splitting the structure is not the same as splitting the thing.

applications.title: Remind the ones who were rescued
applications.text: Alma pressed the point on those who had just been delivered. The people most likely to forget a rescue are the ones who lived through it.

applications.title: Let membership be by desire where you can
applications.text: In a society running on descent, the church ran on wanting in. Ask what your own groups actually require, and whether any of it is inherited rather than chosen.

questions.text: When did I last hear something true that I was not prepared for?
Whom have I not grieved for because the loss was old?
What answer came faster than I expected, and did I say so?
Whose welfare causes me actual pain, and what have I done about it?
What name am I carrying that I have not examined?
What deliverance am I in danger of forgetting?
